title: PM5 Low Battery Warning
shortDescription: PM5 monitor batteries are low and should be replaced soon.
fullDescription:
ERR 05 on the Concept2 PM5 monitor indicates the two D-cell batteries are getting low. While the PM5 also self-charges slightly during rowing, it needs the batteries for boot and persistent memory.

Swap to fresh D cells. Do not mix old and new batteries — the PM5 detects imbalance and may continue showing ERR 05.

fixSteps.title: Replace D cells
fixSteps.instruction: Open battery compartment on back of PM5; replace both D cells with fresh alkaline or rechargeable NiMH.

whenToCallPro: Never — this is a DIY fix.

title: Monitor Not Reading Chain Motion
shortDescription: PM5 isn't detecting the flywheel/chain movement during rowing.
fullDescription:
If the PM5 shows no stroke rate or distance while you row, the magnet pickup sensor on the flywheel isn't registering. The small black sensor inside the housing must be close to (but not touching) the aluminum flywheel.

A loose sensor, damaged sensor cable, or a disturbed sensor after shipping are the common causes.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove flywheel cover; ensure sensor sits ~1mm from flywheel hub, no contact.

videoSearchQuery: Concept2 PM5 no stroke count sensor

faq.a: About 1mm from flywheel — use a business card as spacer.

title: Log Memory Full
shortDescription: PM5 internal log memory is full — delete old workouts.
fullDescription:
ERR 21 means the PM5 has reached its internal storage limit for workout logs. Clear old entries via LogCard or the monitor menu to resume saving.

Consider connecting to ErgData or a USB LogCard to archive before clearing.

fixSteps.title: Archive workouts
fixSteps.instruction: Connect to ErgData app and sync, or insert LogCard and copy.

fixSteps.title: Clear memory
fixSteps.instruction: Menu > More Options > Utilities > Manage Memory > Clear.

faq.a: Yes — via ErgData app or logbook.concept2.com.

title: Bluetooth Connection Failed
shortDescription: PM5 can't pair or maintain Bluetooth Smart connection with phone/watch.
fullDescription:
If Bluetooth pairing to ErgData or a fitness watch fails, first try removing the device from the PM5 pairing list and the phone/watch's Bluetooth list, then re-pair from scratch.

Weak batteries often cause Bluetooth dropouts — try fresh D cells if the issue persists.

fixSteps.title: Clear pairings
fixSteps.instruction: PM5 > Utilities > Wireless > Erase Bluetooth pairings; then forget on phone.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair
fixSteps.instruction: Open ErgData > Add device > follow prompts.

faq.a: Check PM5 > Utilities > Information for firmware version; update via PC Utility.

title: Internal PM5 Error
shortDescription: PM5 encountered an unexpected internal condition — usually clears with a restart.
fullDescription: ERR 01 is a catch-all firmware error. Remove batteries for 30 seconds, reinsert, and reboot PM5. If ERR 01 keeps returning, update firmware via Concept2 PC Utility.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Download Concept2 Utility, connect USB-C, run update.

faq.a: Usually not — logs are in flash memory.

title: USB Communication Failure
shortDescription: PM5 cannot communicate over USB-C to PC utility.
fullDescription:
USB Fail points to cable, driver, or port issues. Try a different USB-C cable (data-capable, not charge-only), another USB port on the PC, or reinstall the Concept2 Utility.

Mac users should have permissions granted; Windows may need a driver reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Swap cable
fixSteps.instruction: Use a known-good data USB-C cable.

whenToCallPro: USB port replacement by Concept2 service.

faq.a: Any USB-C data cable — charge-only cables won't pass data.

title: LogCard Read/Write Error
shortDescription: PM5 cannot read or write to the inserted LogCard.
fullDescription:
The LogCard is a small flash card that plugs into the PM5 for logging and multi-machine use. Corruption can occur if the card is removed mid-write.

Try another card, or format from PC. Concept2 provides a utility to repair LogCards.

fixSteps.title: Reinsert card
fixSteps.instruction: Remove LogCard, wipe contacts with dry cloth, reinsert firmly.

title: Monitor Screen Blank
shortDescription: PM5 screen doesn't wake up at all.
fullDescription:
A completely dead PM5 screen is usually a battery or reset issue. Insert fresh D cells, then press the Menu button to wake the PM5.

If still blank, the monitor may have failed and needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: New batteries
fixSteps.instruction: Install fresh D cells and press Menu.

faq.a: Yes — it mounts with a single thumbscrew.
